newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends slightly up on foreign trend.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends slightly up on foreign trend.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar reversed its early downtrend to close slightly firmer against the U.S. dollar on Thursday on profit-taking overseas on the greenback after its recent gains, dealers said.
The local unit finished at T$27.543, down from an intra-day high of T$27.530, against Wednesday's T$27.557 close. Turnover through dealers was an active US$260 million.
The Taiwan dollar fell to T$27.570 earlier on Thursday, continuing its recent depreciation and reflecting the persistent strength of the American unit in overseas markets.
"But as the U.S. dollar eases against the yen and the mark overseas, profit-taking starts to emerge," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
"The Taiwan dollar should continue to test its lower levels, but it will be a very slow downtrend," the dealer added.
A range of T$27.50-60 was seen in the near term.
